problems: No page failed. Pages opened by the reviewer: Territory of New Guinea, Australian Antarctic Territory, New Guinea campaign, Papua New Guinea, Bougainville Civil War, Australia, Western Samoa Trust Territory, Realm of New Zealand, New Zealand, Republic of Hawaii, New Hebrides, New Caledonia, Territory of Papua, British New Guinea.

Identity question for the orchestrator (not the author's fault): new-zealand starts at the Dominion (26 September 1907) and leaves 1841-1907 to a separate colony-of-new-zealand, although the author's own note calls the Dominion 'the same state as the colony under a new status'. Rule 2 (one dossier and one colour per state; a status change is a rename) argues for one dossier from 1841, with a 1907 rename and the New Zealand Wars as its contests. The brief left pre-1948 New Zealand to oc-02-x, and oc-01's maori-king-movement and united-tribes-of-new-zealand already point at colony-of-new-zealand. Decide before oc-02-x runs: either oc-02-x extends new-zealand back to 1841 (and the oc-01 counterparts are repointed), or the split is confirmed and given one colour.

Consistency question: Papua, the New Guinea mandate and the Territory of Papua and New Guinea (1906-1975) are drawn as direct Australian land (the PNG 1946 Cliopatria shape is verdict wrong), while new-caledonia and new-hebrides are type-colony dossiers that the metropoles hold as a relation. The author flags this. The orchestrator should confirm which convention applies to League and UN territories.

Cross-batch: vanuatu (oc-02-b) has the same coarse Cliopatria shape that I corrected in new-hebrides (28 of 43 land cells); it should use {country: Vanuatu}. kingdom-of-samoa (oc-01) uses german-empire as Samoa's 1900 successor, while new-zealand uses german-samoa: oc-02-x should settle the slug.
